records.quote: Quasi-steady burning corresponding to various condensed-phase materials (such as PMMA and Nylon) was observed in microgravity despite the absence of air flow, where the cessation of ventilation is an established step in putting out spacecraft fires.
records.derivation: Result statement about the ISS flames. PMMA and Nylon are the materials EMULATED, not burned: the burned fuel is a gas (R4-R6). 'Partial-gravity' appears in the documents only as a goal ('to assess the relevance of existing flammability test methods for low and partial-gravity environments', Final Report p.45); no partial-gravity tests exist. Not used as gravity evidence: section=projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' (a category label).

records.quote: We see this as well in the extended ISS microgravity tests.

lineage: BRE shares the ACME chamber insert, cameras and diagnostics in the ISS Combustion Integrated Rack with the other ACME experiments (CLD Flame, E-FIELD Flames, s-Flame, Flame Design, CFI-G; PSI-10, 21, 22, 23 and 159 per the task brief): 'BRE is one of several independent experiments that are part of the ACME project, which uses a single modular set of hardware to carry out studies of flames burning gaseous fuels in the ISS’ Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR).' (Final Report p.45). Round 2 used ACME's standard radiometer array instead of the BRE array (p.18). Shared documents: section 3.A is copied from the 'ACME Engineering Implementation' document (p.7), section 4.B is an excerpt of an E-FIELD Flames paper (p.20), and pages 8-33 of the Data Interpretation PDF carry the header 'ACME/s-Flame Data Interpretation 20 September 2021'. E-FIELD Flames uses an electric field; it is not a gravity data point.
